PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, AND THE PART THAT DIED IS THE HEADLINE. That fact's title says the undeclared-seam finding "can never reach zero" because the two edge sets are "disjoint by construction". IT MOVED TODAY: 8 of 72 covered became 13 of 72, by declaring three contracts between modules that already carried DEPENDS_ON edges.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY TRUE, and the correction is small but changes what follows from it: the sets were disjoint because every contract SAT AT THE SUBSYSTEM BOUNDARY while every coupling sat between MODULES. That is where the contracts happened to be declared, not a property of the schema. "By construction" claims no work can change it; work changed it in an afternoon.

WHAT STILL STANDS, in full and re-measured today:
- 56 of the 64 uncovered pairs have `impl DesignGraph` on BOTH sides and ZERO cross a crate boundary. Its central point — that demanding a contract between two impl blocks of one struct is an alarm on correct work — is unchanged and now independently reproduced.
- Its list of the genuine cmp↔cmp boundaries was right, and the three declared today are additional real ones it did not enumerate rather than corrections to it.
- Its closing sentence is untouched and is still the open question: whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is worth recording at all.

⚠️ SO THE NUMBER CAN MOVE, BUT IT CANNOT REACH ZERO HONESTLY — for the reason the fact gives rather than the one it names. 56 of the remaining pairs should not have contracts at all, so a zero would mean somebody wrote 56 fictions. Anyone reading this as licence to close the gap should read the 56 first.
